bib.title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention

question: Can a sparse attention mechanism be both hardware-efficient across training, prefill and decode and natively trainable, without losing quality against full attention?
hypothesis: Pretraining with hierarchical sparse attention from the start keeps or improves full-attention quality while giving real speedups.
contributions: Hardware-aligned, arithmetic-intensity-balanced blockwise sparse attention kernels (Triton) for speedups.
End-to-end trainable sparse attention with efficient backward operators, reducing pretraining computation without sacrificing performance.

method.summary: NSA replaces full attention with three gated branches (compressed blocks, top-n selected blocks, sliding window) with separate K/V per branch, shared block selection across a GQA group, and Triton kernels. A 27B-total/3B-active GQA+MoE model is pretrained with it and compared with a full-attention twin and inference-time sparse baselines.
